summary: Part 2 of the Planet Labs deep dive (published 2026-09-20) explains why investors are buzzing about the stock: rising geopolitical tension and the company's small-cap leverage to the defense industrial complex, giving it significant upside from current levels. Management's latest call highlighted new contracts including a seven-figure deal with a European defense and intelligence customer for high-resolution global mosaics supporting operational planning. Europe, Middle East, and Africa is the fastest-growing region — unsurprising given Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the Middle East conflicts, and the Strait of Hormuz / Bab al-Mandab blockages driving defense demand. He emphasizes Planet's differentiators: speed of deployment (a first satellite in orbit within 2–4 months of contract award versus years historically), the largest commercial Earth-imaging satellite constellation, and an AI-powered image archive that provides analysis — not just raw imagery — commanding premium prices. He recently started coverage and notes the stock is down meaningfully from the highs reached earlier in the year when anything space-related was hyped around the SpaceX IPO, making it more attractive, though he stops short of a recommendation. Call: PL UNCERTAIN.
